title: Bandbox free breakfasts, Edmond Hall and the $35 scale
summary: Musicians got free breakfast at the Bandbox run by Major; Hall landed a job with Claude Hopkins; Cootie earned $35 a week with Chick.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And -- well, they used to have free breakfasts over there in the Bandbox.
They did? For musicians.
For musicians. They had rolls and coffee.
No kidding.
Sweet rolls and coffee.
Who ran the Bandbox then? Do you remember?
Yeah. A fellow by the name of Major. He ran the Bandbox.
And he liked musicians.
Yeah. He was a trumpet player himself.
Oh.

Eventually he studied to be a lawyer. And so I used to go and get my breakfast, free breakfast every morning. So Edmond Hall -- I think he was still over in Brooklyn -- so Edmond Hall came over on saxophone night, so they heard him.
Playing clarinet.
Playing clarinet and what else -- clarinet and alto I think he was playing. So he got a job with the piano player down at Roseland. What was his name? He was from Washington.
Claude Hopkins.
Claude Hopkins.
Yeah.
He got a job with Claude Hopkins.
Oh, he did.
So he was all straight. So while he -- before he got the job with Claude Hopkins, the little money I was making with Chick, I would help him out.
I see. Yeah. And then did he help out when he got a job, or were you working too?
I was working.
Yeah. Well, you were making $35.00 a week with Chick?
Yeah.
That was scale. At the Savoy.
That was big money during those days.
Yeah. Because Chick was only making $45.00, I think.
Yeah. That was big money. $35.00 a week was a whole lot of money in those days.
